description: Ordered verification gates. Run in order; stop at the first failure. A gate activates with the feature that makes it meaningful — never earlier (a gate that cannot fail teaches nothing) and never later (a gate added after the fact finds a backlog instead of a regression). Gates 1-4 and 6 went active with F-001, after being executed and seen to pass; they were deliberately NOT activated while pnpm install was blocked, because a gate that has never run is theatre. `ciStep: false` means the gate is deliberately covered inside another CI step; the ci-mirror check in verify-state.mjs knows that is intentional. `workflow` names the workflow file a gate is mirrored in, defaulting to .github/workflows/ci.yml — a RELEASE gate runs only when a tag is pushed, and mirroring it against ci.yml would either fail forever or, worse, be dropped from gates.json to make the failure go away.

gates.description: Harness integrity. Validates feature_list.json and effects.json against their schemas; every E-### has a memory note and every memory note is referenced; every effect `to` path exists on disk; every critical link names a guard; wikilinks resolve; wip_limit is respected; blockers are done before a feature is in_progress; an in-flight feature has a plan; every PRD FR/NFR is claimed by a feature and appears in REQUIREMENTS-COVERAGE.md; the ADR index matches the ADR files; gates.json mirrors the CI workflow AND no active gate is conditioned out of it (F-072) — an `if:` on an active gate fails unless gates.json declares a matching ciCondition with a reason of 20+ characters, because this check compares run-commands and used to walk straight past the condition, which is how gate 11 nearly shipped skipped for the whole of R1; scoped rules do not weaken a golden rule; governed-doc relative links resolve.

TypeScript strict typecheck across the workspace. Runs each package's tsconfig.json — the same project the editor and typescript-eslint use — so tests are covered. tsconfig.build.json is the EMIT project only; running the build project here would leave type errors accumulating in files no gate can see.

ESLint 10 flat config, TYPE-AWARE via typescript-eslint against a real TypeScript program (TS 6.0.3 — ADR-0035). Enforces package boundaries, the colour engine platform-freedom rules, no-floating-promises, and later: no colour literals outside the token layer, no hard-coded user-facing strings, the claims copy lint. verify-engine-purity.mjs computes the engine zone as the TRANSITIVE CLOSURE of @irodora/* dependency edges from the declared roots (F-073), not from the color-* naming convention — scoping by name let an engine package depend on a workspace package that imports node:fs with every gate green, which breaks NFR-3 exactly as directly as importing it would. Its --prove run plants three violations including that transitive case and watches each fail, with the clean baseline asserted first and last. ALSO RUNS scripts/verify-guards.mjs, which writes a deliberately violating file at the exact path each rule targets and asserts the rule fires — ten boundaries, proven rather than assumed. A rule nobody has watched fail is not a boundary. NOTE: a later flat-config object REPLACES no-restricted-imports rather than merging, so the workspace patterns are repeated in the colour-engine override; guard #3 exists because that defect shipped once already. ALSO RUNS scripts/verify-claims.mjs — the claims copy lint (NFR-21, ADR-0031, F-025), which is what makes golden rule 11 a gate rather than a habit. It scans every .ts/.tsx/.md/.json in the repository for eleven banned constructions, INCLUDING IDENTIFIERS: an isExactMatch field is as much a violation as a button label, because a name propagates into a record and then into copy. THE PROBLEM THIS GATE HAS is that the banned phrases MUST appear here — ADR-0031 lists them, so do the governance document, three skills and two rule files, and a naive scan flags eighteen files of which most are the policy. A blanket exemption for "documents discussing the policy" would then BE the gate, since every real claim in docs/ sits inside it. So exemptions are three KINDS that are not interchangeable: policySource is an explicit file list (never a glob) with a reason each; an inline claims-ok: marker covers ONE line that forbids the phrase or records its absence, and REQUIRES a reason of 12+ characters — a bare marker is itself a finding, because an exemption nobody had to justify is a way to turn the gate off; and `measured` exempts a real claim, requiring a link to a device-lab row. `measured` IS EMPTY and the gate prints the count on every run, because the device colour lab is F-063 and no number may exist without a row. ACTIVATED after scripts/verify-claims-proof.mjs asserted 14 cases WITH the baseline green either side — 12 that must go red (one per construction, plus a bare marker), and TWO that must stay green: a marker carrying a reason, and the clean fixture. Red is not enough; each case also asserts the output NAMES the right construction, so a gate that fails on everything is distinguishable from one that works. FOUND ON ACTIVATION, and this is the point: the design system's own thesis was "soft chrome, exact colour" — a tagline asserting exactness in a product whose central commitment is that capture is an estimate. It meant the swatch is drawn without a corner radius, which is rendering geometry rather than accuracy, but a two-word thesis migrates into marketing faster than an identifier migrates into a field. Reworded to "soft chrome, unaltered colour", which says what actually happens. Also corrected: three "the true colour" comments in @irodora/corpus derive.ts, now "specified", which is more precise anyway since the value is specified by a corpus entry rather than true in any absolute sense. NOT CHECKED HERE, and printed on every run: the provenance-conditional half of ADR-0031 §1 — whether "measured" sits near an estimated value needs the render tree and activates with F-017. The table is already in claims.json as data.

Prettier formatting check on code and root config. Prose (docs/, .harness/) and byte-significant data (golden datasets, corpus JSON) are excluded — reflowing them makes review diffs unreadable and, for golden data, changes bytes that are compared by hash.

Unit, integration and property-based tests (Vitest + fast-check). Adapter conformance suites went with the ports they conformed to (ADR-0051); the principle they carried survives and applies to the storage layer — a conformance case that cannot fail launders every implementation through it, so each suite must contain at least one case verified to fail against a deliberately broken implementation.

The colour engine against published reference datasets. As of F-006: six cited datasets — the sRGB transfer function (IEC 61966-2-1) weighted at near-black, sRGB and Display-P3 primaries and matrices (CSS Color 4 / SMPTE RP 431-2), CIELAB's exact rationals (CIE 15:2018), Ottosson's published OKLab table, and Lindbloom's Bradford adaptation matrix — plus the cross-platform identity fixture: 10,000 seeded samples × 30 values, digested over IEEE-754 bytes and asserted bit-identical (NFR-3). Every entry declares whether it is a published value, computed from a published formula, or definitional, and an entry citing no source fails the load. F-007 added four more datasets in @irodora/color-difference: all 34 Sharma–Wu–Dalal CIEDE2000 pairs to four decimal places (each ALSO computed independently by culori, so a transcription error in the reference data is caught separately from an implementation error), WCAG contrast against its worked examples with every constant pinned digit-for-digit, APCA 0.0.98G-4g asserted BITWISE against colorjs.io, and a second determinism digest over the metrics — which is where a cross-engine divergence would appear first, since CIEDE2000 alone calls atan2, exp, sin, cos and pow. CVD confusion-line pairs join with F-008. Activated after being executed AND after each dataset was watched reject a real mutation: a pure-power transfer function, a column-swapped matrix (which leaves white BIT-identical), decimal-rounded ε and κ, and a 2% perturbation of any OKLab matrix element. A changed golden value requires an ADR — it is a claim about physical reality. The identity digest is a determinism fixture rather than such a claim, and regenerating it to make a test green is the one thing it exists to prevent. F-009 added the gamut dataset: 14 entries mapping out-of-gamut colours into sRGB by OKLCh chroma reduction. Every entry is DEFINITIONAL rather than a published value, because no published table of mapped results exists — so the test asserts the DEFINITION directly: the result is in gamut AND one bisection step more chroma is not, so an entry cannot pass by the implementation agreeing with itself. Cross-checked against culori clampChroma (agreement 0.0063 dE00, an independent implementation of the same algorithm) and deliberately NOT against colorjs.io toGamut({method:"css"}), which is a different algorithm — CSS Color 4 with a MINDE early stop that disagrees by up to 5.21 dE00 and drifts hue up to 11.97 degrees (ADR-0045). The decoy is per-channel clipping, implemented in the test and measured at 33.6 degrees of hue shift, with our own drift asserted beside it as the baseline.
Turborepo build of every package and app.

End-to-end against the running app. The API half of this charter was retired with the server tier (ADR-0051); the app half lands with apps/mobile and covers the human journeys, a simulated-CVD journey, and the assertion that a Lens scan transmits no bytes at all (NFR-12) — which on a local-first app is checkable as "the process opens no socket" rather than "the request carried no image". `pnpm test:e2e` runs scripts/e2e-scope.mjs FIRST, which FAILS if no package declares a test:e2e script and otherwise prints each charter item as covered or NOT COVERED with the file that would supply it. That report is what stops a green gate being read as coverage that does not exist. NOTE the reason this gate is `pending` with ciStep:false: nothing declares test:e2e today, and e2e-scope.mjs exits non-zero on that by design. A gate that cannot pass is not the same as a gate that fails open, but it still stops the build, so the CI step is withdrawn until its subject exists rather than being guarded by an `if:` — which is the F-072 hazard, and would leave the gate reading `active` in gates.json while never once running. ciStep:false and status:pending both flip back with F-039, together, and the mirror check enforces that pairing.

Accessibility for every component and every screen — zero violations, not warnings. React Native exposes this through the platform accessibility APIs rather than the DOM, so axe cannot run (ADR-0051 retired the web surface; ADR-0055 chose what replaces it). The check renders under jest-expo and asserts over the accessibility TREE: roles, accessible names, states, tap-target DECLARATIONS, font scaling, and that every rendered colour resolves to a manifest token. scripts/a11y-scope.mjs runs first and fails if any component is unreachable from a conformance registry, because a suite that passes over a component nobody registered proves nothing about it. IT DOES NOT PROVE THE PIXELS: there is no Yoga layout in a JS render tree, so clipping at 200%, overflow, occlusion and measured tap-target size are invisible to it and stay attested on F-017.

Reads docs/design/design-system.manifest.json and asserts, in BOTH themes: every declared `pairsWith` combination meets the WCAG 2.2 AA minimum its `usage` selects, with APCA Lc reported alongside and never substituted (ADR-0021); every `srgb` value matches what the engine derives from that token OKLCh (ADR-0043); the chroma ceiling, with every exception recorded in the manifest rather than carved into the checker; and the structural rules carrying NFR-9. A pairing used in a component but absent from `pairsWith` is a failure — the declaration is how the gate knows what to check. Report-only while the manifest status is `placeholder`, blocking once it is `approved`; that switch is read from the manifest, not hard-coded. The arithmetic is NOT in the gate script: checkContrast/checkChromaCeiling/checkStructure live in @irodora/design-tokens so the gate and the tests run the same code, and every colour number under them comes from @irodora/color-difference. Translucent tokens are composited in LINEAR light over EVERY ground they declare, and judged on the worst — naming one favourable ground is how a check passes a border that is invisible where it is used. ACTIVATED after being watched fail on five real defects in the approved manifest, and after scripts/verify-contrast-proof.mjs asserted nine cases WITH the baseline green in each — six red: a token nudged below AA, a hand-edited hex, a removed chroma exception, a collapsed cvdPair, the status icon channel made optional (typecheck), and an emitter changed without regenerating; plus ONE that must stay green — a placeholder manifest status with a real failure present, which proves the report-only switch works in the direction that would otherwise look exactly like a passing build. THE COLOUR-SCIENCE REVIEW CHANGED WHAT THIS GATE CHECKS: translucent tokens are now evaluated under BOTH the linear-light and the encoded compositing model and judged on the worse, because neither is uniformly stricter and the encoded one is what a browser actually draws; the CVD half evaluates ALL ELEVEN tabulated Machado severities rather than only 1.0, because Machado is not monotone in severity; it also evaluates Vienot total dichromacy for protan and deutan, because color-engine.md assigns total dichromacy to Vienot and the two models disagree by up to 5.6 points; and a token that no declared pairing covers is now a FAILURE unless it carries an `uncheckedReason`, because gate scope is driven by pairsWith and an unchecked token was previously indistinguishable from a passing one. The first cvdPair decoy did NOT discriminate — it was written against earlier token values and stopped collapsing the pair once status.warn moved, passing with the mutation applied; it was replaced with a 48-degree hue rotation that takes the pair from 64.1 to 31.8. THE RE-MEASUREMENT WAS ITSELF STALE for a while — the prose said 65.2 to 30.0 after the values moved again, which is the same defect one level up, and it was caught by the F-003 evaluation rather than by anything automatic. NOT IMPLEMENTED HERE: the half of this charter that scans RENDERED surfaces for colour-only status indicators. No component exists until F-017, and the gate says so on every run rather than implying coverage by being green. THE F-003 EVALUATION FOUND THE PROOF HAD A HOLE: no mutation isolated checkContrast, because the one contrast mutation also broke the ADR-0043 derived-hex check — so a checkContrast returning passes:true unconditionally left gate 9 exiting 0 and every other mutation green. Verified by neutering it. Case 8 now mutates the comparison itself and checks the PACKAGE TESTS rather than gate 9, because gate 9 alone genuinely does not catch it; test/check.test.ts covers the same ground with an independently recomputed ratio. F-067 CLOSED IT: gate 9 now also asserts checkSalience — the RECORDED salience rank of the status tokens, measured as |APCA Lc| against each theme own background. The rank is read from the manifest rather than derived from the values, because a rank derived from the values can never disagree with them, which is the state the defect shipped in. The defect: light ranked bad 89.3 > warn 73.4 > ok 72.7 while dark ranked warn 60.8 > ok 56.8 > bad 38.6, so a person toggling the theme was told a different state was urgent — and dark.status.bad sat at |Lc| 37.5 against the Lc 45 large-text floor while WCAG read 4.92 and passed. ADR-0053 moves the three dark status tokens: worst |Lc| 37.5 -> 46.5, worst CVD separation 65.2 -> 63.1, and error becomes the loudest state in both themes at the cost of reading as pale pink in dark. Proven by a tenth mutation case that swaps two entries in the recorded rank.

Colour-vision-deficiency regression, and the accessibility promise (NFR-10). Split from gate 5 deliberately: gate 5 asks whether the models reproduce their published values; this asks whether a pairing the product would recommend stays distinguishable — and that must be able to go red on its own. As of F-008 it covers the separation score shape: bounds, exact-zero identity, symmetry, severity clamping, severity-0 equivalence across deficiencies, monotonic degradation of a red-green pair, and the false negative the lightness term exists to avoid. ACTIVATED after being watched fail — deleting the lightness term from separation.ts makes it exit 1, restoring it exits 0. The FIRST version of that decoy did not discriminate: it used a pair where both terms saturate, and the gate passed with the term deleted. It was replaced with a pair where the term contributes 14.6 points, and the binding frequency (~9% of sampled pairs) is asserted so the case is not hand-picked. The design system cvdPairs assertion joins with F-003.

Corpus integrity (NFR-20). Fails the build if ANY record lacks source, sourceType, sourceLicence, derivation, authoredBy, verifiedBy or verifiedAt; if author and reviewer are the same identity — checked as ROSTER IDS against content/editors.json, because a free-text name comparison passes "A. Ranjan" against "Ashish Ranjan" and launders an unreviewed entry (ADR-0047); if a historical classification has no dated primary source; if a record whose sourceType is editorial carries ANY classification other than japanese-inspired or editorial — not merely historical, because traditional claims the received canon and modern-japanese claims documented current practice, and neither is ours to assert; if a derived value in the LATEST published bundle is inconsistent with its xyz under the CURRENT engine (this is the destination half of E-001, unguarded until now); if a palette has no anchor; if a relation points at a missing slug; if a published entry differs from its checksum; if a slug is duplicated; if a null carries no reason in unknowns, or a reason names a field that is not null (FR-21, both directions); or if a cited source is absent from the licensing-and-provenance.md §5 register — a check that document already asserted existed and did not. An UNPARSEABLE register is a FAILURE, never an absence of constraint. There is no partial publication. THE PROBLEM THIS GATE HAS: F-011 ships it and F-012 ships the entries, so on activation content/colors/ is EMPTY and a gate that passes over nothing is failing open. Four things answer that: it FAILS if it cannot locate its inputs (corpus root, roster, register, fixtures) rather than passing over an empty set; it runs 1 valid + 18 invalid FIXTURE corpora on every invocation so the rules exercised are never zero, and THE VALID ONE CARRIES A PUBLISHED BUNDLE — without which the checksum, ledger and E-001 destination rules are correct code that never runs, which is how they shipped at first and what an evaluation caught by putting a throw at the top of the loop and watching the gate stay green; the fixtures cannot become content (they live under packages/, the scan globs content/ only, and a fixture- slug under content/ is itself a failure); and scripts/verify-content-proof.mjs mutates the VALID fixture corpus 25 ways and asserts the gate goes red AND NAMES THE RIGHT FIELD, with the baseline asserted green before and after every case. Five attack the published bundle (edited entry, edited derived value, altered ledger checksum, removed ledger row, removed entry — that last being the case per-entry digests cannot catch, which is why there are two digest levels). One perturbs XYZ_TO_LMS_OKLAB by 0.01 and REBUILDS the engine, which is the E-001 destination check as its effect link describes it; that case did not exist when the link first claimed it did, and an evaluation caught the false claim by running the experiment. ONE case must stay GREEN — an entry reordered and reformatted — because a proof where everything is red cannot distinguish a working gate from one that fails on everything. Activated after all 19 cases were WATCHED. Building the fixtures found two defects in the fixtures themselves: the duplicate-slug case was broken in two ways and failed for the wrong rule, then, once fixed, wrote both entries to one filename and stopped being invalid at all. Both were caught by the gate, not by review. NOT CHECKED HERE, and printed on every run: that a human READ an entry (F-012 owes that as an attested criterion), and an edit to a published entry made together with a matching ledger update — a two-file diff caught by review and by nothing else — there is no publish path beyond the pull request (ADR-0051). The authored-entry count is printed beside the fixture rule count so a green run over an empty corpus cannot be read as coverage.

Performance against ABSOLUTE committed thresholds (NFR-4), never baseline deltas — hardware varies, and a delta gate flakes until someone disables it. Every threshold is now on-device: live pick <= 50 ms perceived, local analysis p95 <= 200 ms, recommendation p95 <= 200 ms, capsule solve (40 garments) p95 <= 3 s. The API p95 <= 300 ms budget went with the API (ADR-0051). A miss is a tracked work item, never an edited threshold.

Secret scanning (gitleaks 8.30.1, pinned) and dependency audit. A Critical or High advisory blocks release (`pnpm audit --audit-level high`). A gitleaks finding ROTATES the secret — it never earns an allowlist entry, because a secret in git history is compromised regardless of whether the commit was pushed. CI installs the pinned binary and invokes THIS command rather than using gitleaks-action, so a workstation scan and a CI scan are the same scan. Activated after being executed (7 commits, no leaks) AND after its ruleset was watched fire on planted secrets outside git history — 3 of 4 shapes detected, exit 1. Note that gitleaks' default rules deliberately allowlist published example credentials such as AWS's AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE; a scan that stays green on those is correct, not broken. F-079 CHANGED TWO THINGS. FIRST, the gate is ONE command: `pnpm security` runs the secret scan and then the advisory check. It used to be two CI steps of which only the first was mirrored against gates.json, so the dependency audit could have been deleted with every gate still reading as covered — F-078’s defect in a different directory. SECOND, the audit verdict moved into scripts/verify-audit.mjs, because `pnpm audit --audit-level high` had exited 1 on EVERY run since F-039 and a permanently red gate is a gate nobody reads. Two HIGH advisories against image-size have NO FIXED VERSION — latest published is 2.0.2 and both cover <=2.0.2 with first_patched_version null — so there was never an upgrade or an override available, only the choice between leaving it red and writing down a disposition. The rule now: a blocking advisory either stops the build, or it is in .harness/verification/advisories.json with a reachability argument of 80+ characters, a named owner, an ADR and an EXPIRY. Deliberately NOT pnpm’s own auditConfig.ignoreGhsas, which is one line and carries no expiry, no owner and no reason — an entry added under deadline pressure would be indistinguishable from one that was thought about, and silent for years. THREE WAYS IT GOES RED, and the third is the point: a blocking advisory absent from the register; an entry past its expiry, which stops working by itself because an expiry someone has to remember is not one; and an entry matching nothing in today’s report, because a dead exception is how a live one gets waved through later. ACTIVATED after being watched: the register was committed EMPTY first and seen to fail on both real advisories, then verify-audit.mjs --prove asserted 11 cases — 8 red, including a DIFFERENT high advisory failing while an accepted one is in force (the acceptance criterion that stops an entry becoming a blanket exemption), and 3 that must stay GREEN including a moderate advisory nobody accepted. NOT CHECKED HERE, and printed on every run: whether the vulnerable code is REACHABLE. That needs call-graph analysis this repository does not have, which is exactly why every acceptance rests on a written argument carrying an owner and a date rather than a tick.

The BUILT ARTEFACT must prove its own claims, rather than the configuration that produced it being trusted to have produced them. Reads the APK directly — the ZIP central directory, the binary AndroidManifest.xml resource chunk, and the v2/v3 APK Signing Block — and asserts: android.permission.INTERNET is ABSENT (NFR-12 as a property of the shipped file), the package id is com.irodora.app, versionCode and versionName match what the tag asked for, and for a release build the signer certificate SHA-256 matches the fingerprint the workflow expects. THE REASON THIS IS A GATE AND NOT A COMMENT IN THE WORKFLOW: app.config.ts blocks INTERNET today, and a config plugin, a dependency, or an Expo template change can put it back — the manifest merger adds permissions silently and by design. Every other check in this repository looks at source; this one is the only thing that looks at what a person would actually install. It runs in release.yml rather than ci.yml because there is no APK on a pull request; gates.json records that with `workflow`, and gate 0 mirrors it there, so deleting the step fails gate 0 exactly as deleting a ci.yml step does. PROVEN by scripts/verify-apk.mjs --prove, which assembles synthetic APKs — one declaring INTERNET, one with a wrong package id, one with a mismatched versionCode, one unsigned — and watches each go red, with a clean synthetic APK asserted GREEN before and after, because a proof where everything is red cannot distinguish a working checker from one that fails on everything. NOT CHECKED HERE, and printed on every run: that the app opens no socket at RUNTIME. A permission it does not hold is a stronger fact than a promise, but it is not the same fact — that half is gate 7 on a device, and stays attested on F-039.
